title: Chapter 10 – FIDE Arbiter Regulations: Mock Exam

questions.text: What are the two FIDE arbiter titles?
questions.explanation: As per Article B06.1.1, FIDE awards two arbiter titles: FIDE Arbiter (FA) and International Arbiter (IA). Both are awarded for life unless revoked.

questions.text: What minimum exam score must a candidate achieve to qualify for the FA title?
questions.explanation: As per Article B06.1.3, to be awarded the FIDE Arbiter title, a candidate must pass a FIDE Arbiter seminar exam with a score of at least 80%.

options.text: Any norm scored at a national championship
A norm scored at top-level events like Olympiad or World Championship
The first norm achieved by any arbiter
A norm scored by a Category A arbiter

questions.explanation: As per Article B06.1.2, an A-norm is the highest grade of arbiter norm, awarded for serving at top-level events such as the Olympiad, World Championship, or Continental Championship.

questions.text: What additional requirement must an IA candidate meet that an FA candidate does not?

options.text: Must hold a FIDE player title
Must demonstrate proficiency in a FIDE official language
Must have organised at least one tournament
Must pass a more difficult written exam

questions.explanation: As per Article B06.1.4, among other requirements, IA candidates must demonstrate proficiency in a FIDE official language. This requirement does not apply to the FA title.

questions.text: What sanctions can the ARB Disciplinary Sub-Committee NOT impose on an arbiter?

options.text: A financial fine payable to the opposing players

questions.explanation: As per Article B06.5.4, the available sanctions are: warning, suspension from arbiting, downgrading of classification, suspension of title, and revocation of title. A financial fine payable to players is not a listed sanction.
